newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Home mortgage loans continue to grow in Dec - HKMA.
newsitem.headline: Home mortgage loans continue to grow in Dec - HKMA.

text.p: The volume of residential mortgage loans in Hong Kong continued to grow in December, Hong Kong Monetary Authority data showed on Tuesday.
The HKMA said in a statement total outstanding mortgage lending by the 33 institutions in the survey rose by 2.4 percent to HK$330.4 billion.
The growth rate was higher than the monthly average of 1.6 percent over the last 12 months, it said.

"The rapid growth in lending reflected the increased activity in both the primary and secondary residential property markets in November," HKMA deputy chief executive David Carse said in the statement.
The 12-month average of outstanding loans showed an annualised growth rate of 18.9 percent, compared with 17.6 percent in November, it said.
The amount of new loans approved but not yet drawn dropped from the already high base in November by 8.4 percent to HK$12.7 billion in December.

"In view of the buoyancy of the residential property market and new flats offered to the market in early January, we expect the growth of residential mortgage loans will continue to rise quite rapidly in January," Carse said.
Lending for the purchase of properties in China increased by 4.4 percent to HK$6.3 billion in December.
Gross loans made in December increased both in number, from 178 to 310, and in amount, from $161 million to $401 million.
New loans approved in December decreased both in number from 246 to 212, and in amount from $272 million to $156 million.
